newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian public/private unions eye general strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian public/private unions eye general strike.

text.p: Union leaders heading Colombia's six-day-old national public sector strike will meet their private sector counterparts Monday to plan joint action and a possible general strike, the head of the main state workers' union FENALTRASE said Sunday.

FENALTRASE chief Wilson Borja said the aim of the joint public-private sector action would be to paralyze national production and force the government to cede on labor demands for higher pay and to abandon part of its neoliberal economic policy.
"We will be meeting with the main private sector unions Monday and looking for ways that the private sector can support the nationwide public sector strike," Borja said.
"We have said that if the government doesn't resolve our demands then we must take steps to paralyze national production. A general strike may not be imminent but it is in our sights," he added.

Public sector employees called a strike to press for a 21.5 percent pay hike, compared to the government's sub-inflation, weighted 13.5 percent offer. They are also protesting at a planned wave of privatizations and what they say is a repressive labor code.

Colombia's three main labor federations have both public and private sector affiliates. But so far non-state workers, themselves disgruntled at a below-inflation rise in the minimum wage, have not taken any direct role in the state workers' strike.
No firm time has been set for the resumption of talks between union leaders and government ministers but Borja said both sides could meet Sunday evening.
